   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">Outfitter leases office space located at <em style="font: inherit;">2727</em> Old Elm Hill Pike, Nashville, Tennessee (the &#8220;Nashville Lease&#8221;). The lease commenced in <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2024 </em>and originally had a contractual expiration date of <em style="font: inherit;"> April 2026. </em>The lease agreement required monthly lease payments of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771443" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-OutfitterSatelliteIncMember_LeaseContractualTermAxis-LeaseFor2727OldElmHillPikeNashvilleTennesseeMember" unitRef="USD" name="nxpl:OperatingLeaseMonthlyPayment" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4,800</ix:nonFraction>. In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the Company executed a First Amendment to the lease agreement extending the lease term through <em style="font: inherit;"> April 1, 2027 </em>and revising lease payments effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2026. </em>In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">842,</em> the amendment was evaluated as a lease modification. As the modification extended the lease term and revised future lease payments without granting an additional right-of-use separate from the original lease, the Company accounted for the amendment as a modification of the existing operating lease. Accordingly, the Company remeasured the operating lease liability as of the modification date using a revised discount rate, with a corresponding adjustment recorded to the related right-of-use asset.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Progressive Care entered into a lease agreement for its Orlando pharmacy in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2020. </em>The term of the lease is <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2020-08-31_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-ProgressiveCareMember_LeaseContractualTermAxis-OrlandoPharmacyMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142771445" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">66</ix:nonNumeric> months with a termination date of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2026. </em>The lease agreement calls for monthly payments that began in <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2021, </em>of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771446" contextRef="d_2020-08-01_2020-08-31_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-ProgressiveCareMember_LeaseContractualTermAxis-OrlandoPharmacyMember" unitRef="USD" name="nxpl:OperatingLeaseMonthlyPayment" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">4,310</ix:nonFraction>, with an escalating payment schedule each year thereafter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Progressive Care leases its North Miami Beach pharmacy location under an operating lease agreement with a lease commencement date in <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2021. </em>The term of the lease is <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2021-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-ProgressiveCareMember_LeaseContractualTermAxis-NorthMiamiBeachPharmacyMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c142771447" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">60</ix:nonNumeric> months with a termination date in <em style="font: inherit;"> August 2026. </em>The lease calls for monthly payments of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771448" contextRef="d_2021-09-01_2021-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-ProgressiveCareMember_LeaseContractualTermAxis-NorthMiamiBeachPharmacyMember" unitRef="USD" name="nxpl:OperatingLeaseMonthlyPayment" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">5,237</ix:nonFraction>, with an escalating payment schedule each year thereafter.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Variable expenses generally represent the Company&#8217;s share of the landlord&#8217;s operating expenses.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">Right-of-use assets for operating leases are periodically reduced by impairment losses. We use the long-lived assets impairment guidance in ASC Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">360</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> Property, Plant, and Equipment &#8211; Overall, to determine whether an ROU asset is impaired, and if so, the amount of the impairment loss to recognize. For the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>the Company recorded approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771451" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseImpairmentLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million of impairment loss related to the write-down of a&#160;right-of-use asset as a result of taking the leased equipment out of service and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> returning to service in the future. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impairments related to the write-down of right-of-use assets for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">
     &#160;
   </div>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">
     We monitor for events or changes in circumstances that require a reassessment of
    <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of our leases. When a reassessment results in the re-measurement of a lease liability, a corresponding adjustment is made to the carrying amount of the corresponding ROU asset unless doing so would reduce the carrying amount of the ROU asset to an amount less than zero. In that case, the amount of the adjustment that would result in a negative ROU asset balance is recorded in profit or loss.
   </div>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">20.</em></b>&#160;<b> Reportable Segments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142771458"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142771588">two</span></span>&#160;reportable segments: (i) e-Commerce Operations, which involves acquiring and leasing, primarily an e-commerce platform to collaborate with businesses to optimize their ability to sell their goods online, domestically, and internationally, and enabling customers and partners to optimize their e-commerce presence and revenue, and other related businesses and (ii) Healthcare Operations, which provides TPA, data management, COVID-<em style="font: inherit;">19</em> related diagnostics and vaccinations, prescription pharmaceuticals, compounded medications, telepharmacy services, anti-retroviral medications, medication therapy management, the supply of prescription medications to long-term care facilities, medication adherence packaging, contracted pharmacy&#160;services for <em style="font: inherit;">340B</em> covered entities under the <em style="font: inherit;">340B</em> Drug Discount Pricing Program, and health practice risk management.&#160;This organizational structure aligns with how the Company&#8217;s CODMs manage the business, including resource allocation and performance assessment, and further aligns with the Company&#8217;s product categories and the key markets the Company serves.</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The CODMs include the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The CODMs do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> review segment assets and segment expenses at a level different than what is reported in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets and Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Loss.&#160;While the Company believes there are synergies between the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;reportable segments, the segments are managed separately because each requires different business strategies.&#160;Accounting policies associated with our operating segments are generally the same as those described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em></p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3153149" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">21.</em> Commitments and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;"><b><i>Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> March 17, 2025, </em>a former employee of Pharmco LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, filed a lawsuit against Pharmco LLC, asserting claims under the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) regulations.&#160;On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 14, 2025, </em>the Company reached a Settlement Agreement with the plaintiff to resolve all claims. The settlement was fully covered by the Company&#8217;s insurance policy, and the insurer remitted payment directly to the plaintiff on the Company&#8217;s behalf.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 28, 2024, </em>Alan Jay Weisberg, the former Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of Progressive Care Inc. (&#8220;RXMD&#8221;), filed a putative class action suit on behalf of himself and all other former RXMD stockholders against NextPlat, Charles M. Fernandez, the former Chief Executive Officer and&#160;director of NextPlat, and Rodney Barreto, a director of NextPlat. The complaint purports to allege a breach of fiduciary duty by NextPlat and Messrs. Fernandez and Barreto in connection with the merger of RXMD with and into a wholly owned subsidiary of NextPlat (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;), which Merger was completed on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2024 </em>following approval by the stockholders of each of NextPlat and RXMD in stockholder meetings held on <em style="font: inherit;"> September 13, 2024 </em>by NextPlat and RXMD, respectively. Among other things, the complaint asserts that the consideration paid to Mr. Weisberg and the other RXMD stockholders in connection with the Merger was insufficient.&#160;The monetary relief requested in the complaint includes compensatory and rescissory damages in an unspecified dollar amount.&#160;The complaint is pending in the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware. The caption is<i> Alan Jay Weisberg v. Charles M. Fernandez, Rodney Barreto and Nextplat Corp.,</i> and the case number is C.A. <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">20.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">24</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">1097</em>-MTZ.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company believes the claims asserted in the action are without merit and intends to continue to vigorously defend against the lawsuit. The Company has filed a motion to dismiss the complaint. Although the parties have engaged in discussions regarding a potential resolution of the matter, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> agreement has been reached and there can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that the matter will be resolved on acceptable terms or at all. Based on currently available information and after consultation with legal counsel, management determined that a loss associated with this matter is probable and reasonably estimable in accordance with applicable accounting guidance. Accordingly, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company recorded an accrual of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771474" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_LitigationCaseAxis-FormerCeoOfProgressiveCareLitigationCaseMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.75</ix:nonFraction> million,&#160;which represents management&#8217;s current estimate of loss exposure and corresponds to the Company&#8217;s applicable insurance retention under its directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance coverage.&#160;Due to the significant and unusual nature of the contingent loss accrual, the Company classified the associated expense within other (expense) income instead of operating expenses (as with other legal settlements) as to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> distort operating losses.&#160;The ultimate outcome of the matter remains uncertain, and the actual loss could differ materially from the amount accrued. Any such difference could have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows in the period in which the matter is resolved.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 17, 2024, </em>Progressive Care was notified of a potential claim that&#160;a former employee&#160;(the &#8220;Claimant&#8221;) allegedly suffered a loss due to an alleged breach by Progressive Care of an employment contract with the Claimant.&#160;On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 7, 2025, </em>Progressive Care entered into a Settlement Agreement (the &#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;) with the Claimant to resolve all disputes related to the employment and the arbitration proceeding. Pursuant to the Settlement Agreement, Progressive Care paid the Claimant a total sum of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771476" contextRef="d_2025-11-07_2025-11-07_LitigationCaseAxis-EmploymentAndArbitrationProceedingMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsForLegalSettlements" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">150,000</ix:nonFraction> within <em style="font: inherit;">seven</em> days of execution. In addition, Progressive Care transferred to the Claimant <ix:nonFraction id="c142771478" contextRef="d_2025-11-07_2025-11-07_LitigationCaseAxis-EmploymentAndArbitrationProceedingMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="Share" name="nxpl:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesLitigationSettlement" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">128,205</ix:nonFraction> shares of NextPlat common stock&#160;valued at $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771479" contextRef="d_2025-11-07_2025-11-07_LitigationCaseAxis-EmploymentAndArbitrationProceedingMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="nxpl:StockIssuedDuringPeriodValueLitigationSettlement" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100,000</ix:nonFraction>. The Settlement Agreement provides the Claimant&#160;with a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-time reverse stock-split protection mechanism, whereby, if the aggregate value of the transferred shares declines by more than <em style="font: inherit;">20%</em> within <em style="font: inherit;">sixty</em> calendar days following a reverse stock split, Progressive Care will issue additional shares of NextPlat common stock to the Claimant to restore the aggregate value to the pre-split level, with such shares to be issued within <em style="font: inherit;">ten</em> days after the <em style="font: inherit;">sixty</em>-day period.&#160;The settlement amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771485" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_LitigationCaseAxis-EmploymentAndArbitrationProceedingMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GainLossRelatedToLitigationSettlement" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF" sign="-">250,000</ix:nonFraction> is included in &#8220;Loss on settlement of litigation&#8221; in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive Loss.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">From time to time, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>become involved in litigation relating to claims arising out of our operations in the normal course of business. Other than the matter described above, the Company is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently involved in any pending legal proceeding, claims or litigation, and to the best of our knowledge, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> governmental authority is contemplating any proceeding to which the Company is a party or to which any of the Company&#8217;s properties is subject, which would reasonably be likely to have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">22.</em> Related Party Transactions</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company uses an American Express account for Orbital Satcom and an American Express account for GTC, both in the name of the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer,&#160;who personally guarantees the balance owed. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the accounts payable due to related party includes amounts&#160;due to the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer.&#160;Total related party payments due as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em> were $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771490" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-DavidPhippsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsPayableCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142771491" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-DavidPhippsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsPayableCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">18,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively. Those related party payables are non-interest bearing and due on demand.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">During the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the Company employed and paid wages to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> employee&#160;related to the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> employee&#160;related to the Company&#8217;s Chief Financial Officer.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: justify;">During the year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company employed&#160;and paid wages to the spouse of the Company&#8217;s&#160;late Chief Executive Officer, Charles M. Fernandez, as Chief of Staff and Special Assistant to the Chairman of the Board. The Company terminated Mrs. Fernandez&#8217;s employment with the Company on <em style="font: inherit;"> August 13, 2025.</em></p>
